title: Set a circular saw's blade depth for the board under it: hold the falling motor so one tooth shows below, then lock
instruction: Set the saw's cutting depth for the board it is sitting on, lock it, and let go of the saw.
context: Carpenters (O*NET 47-2031, about 940,000 US jobs) cut sheathing, decking and framing with 7-1/4 in circular saws and reset the blade depth whenever the stock changes. The rule taught on site: the teeth 1/8 to 1/4 in (3.2 to 6.4 mm) below the stock, about one tooth; more exposed blade raises kickback and injury risk, less does not cut through cleanly. Here a DeWalt DWE575-class saw (4.0 kg, unplugged) sits on the board with its blade just past the board's near edge, so the teeth can be seen against the edge face. The board is one of six common stocks and the depth is wherever the last job left it. The depth lever clamps the motor to its bracket; released, the 3.4 kg motor and blade hang on the front pivot (about 19 N at the rear handle) and fall to full depth unless the handle is held. Locking clamps the depth wherever the blade is at that moment, so one hand holds the depth while the other locks.
setup: Station table in front of two YAM arms (bases 61 cm apart), overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robot's left of their midpoint. Two 2x3 offcuts on edge (3.8 x 6.35 x 18 cm, long side along x) stand on the table at y -25 and +25, centred at x 43.3. On them lies one board, 14 cm wide (x 36.3 to 50.3) and 60 cm long along y: 1/4 in tempered hardboard (6.4 mm), 15/32 in plywood (11.9 mm), 23/32 in plywood (18.3 mm), a 5/4 x 6 deck board (25.4 mm), a 2x6 (38.1 mm) or 1-3/4 in LVL (44.5 mm). On the board sits an unplugged 7-1/4 in DeWalt DWE575-class circular saw (4.0 kg, 24-tooth blade): front toward the robot's right (-y), blade side toward the robot, blade plane at x 35.5 (8 mm outside the board's near edge), shoe centre at y -6; its red depth lever (on the depth bracket behind the upper guard, blade side) is locked. Each trial draws from its seed, independently: the board (uniformly over the six), the start depth (the saw left fully raised, blade 0-2 mm below the shoe, or fully lowered, 59.5-64 mm; 1/2 each) and a shift of the saw along the board of up to 1.2 cm. Named check setups (real trials use these): 23/32 ply, depth 62 mm; 2x6, 1 mm; 15/32 ply, 61 mm; deck board, 0 mm; LVL, 63 mm; hardboard, 60 mm (depth = blade below the shoe, on the saw's scale). The screenshot shows the default trial seed: deck board, saw fully raised (0.2 mm).
scoring: Read at the end of the trial (person check in brackets). 1.0 (ends the trial): lowest tooth 1/8 to 1/4 in (3.2 to 6.4 mm) below the board's underside (steel rule against the board's edge face beside the blade), depth lever locked (lever down on its stop; the motor does not move under a light push on the rear handle), shoe flat on the board (no rock, no gap), both hands 5 cm or more from the saw, saw still for 1 s. 0.4: the same but the tooth 1 to 3.2 mm or 6.4 to 9 mm below the underside. 0: lever released (the motor then drops to full depth by itself), tooth above the underside or more than 9 mm below it, shoe not flat on the board, or a hand still on the saw; and 0 for the whole trial if at any time the saw tipped more than 10 deg or fell off the board (video). Sim: tooth position from the blade's pose; lever locked = within 6 deg of its stop (where its cam clamps); flat = within 1 deg and 1.5 mm.
reset_notes: Unlock the lever, set the start depth for the next setup on the saw's depth scale (blade above or below the board's underside as listed), lock, and put the next setup's board on the blocks; set the saw on it, front to the robot's right, blade side toward the robot, blade 8 mm outside the board's near edge. Setups run in order 0-5.
fidelity: Isaac Lab-Arena yam_arena, PhysX (CPU) 480 Hz, 20 Hz control, full size. Saw: one articulation (shoe; 3.4 kg motor and blade on the depth pivot; lever), representative geometry from published DWE575 figures (internal layout estimated). Clamp: pivot drive anchored when the lever closes, capped at 25 N m (slips beyond); the cam lever flips at about 10 N. Lower blade guard not modelled. Boards kinematic. No welds, snaps or proximity rules. Full statement: README.
run_limit: 2400 control steps (2 min at 20 Hz). The trial also ends as soon as the score reaches 1.0.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (seed 0, 2,400 steps). Scripted demo: 1.0 in the official run (default seed, 629/2,400 steps); 1.0 twice, identical; 1.0 at other starts. Doing nothing: 0. Lever left released, wrong-board depth or no hand on handle: 0. Open-loop replay, other board or start side: 0.
